modules.name: ridu
modules.summary: Configure a Ridu application, start its server, and define access rules.

symbols.name: New
symbols.summary: Create an application from config and a document store.
symbols.signature: func New(applicationConfig Config, backend store.Store) (*App, error)
details: When compiled by ridu build, the application carries the exact ordered migration-history fingerprint used by official adapter readiness. Application-owned servers remain responsible for running readiness before admitting traffic.

symbols.name: Resolve
symbols.summary: Resolve executable config into a deterministic schema manifest.
details: Resolution runs plugin transforms without opening a database.

symbols.name: Execute
symbols.summary: Run the API, admin, jobs, and shutdown lifecycle.

parameters.name: applicationConfig
parameters.description: Executable collections, globals, plugins, tasks, and application policy.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Runtime infrastructure and framework-owned server settings.

returns.description: The first joined project-command, startup, serving, drain, or cleanup failure.

details: With project-command arguments, Execute resolves config and runs the versioned CLI protocol without applying runtime options or opening adapters. With no arguments, it starts the framework-owned HTTP server and requires WithStore.

Server startup opens the document store, opens optional upload storage, constructs the application, verifies readiness, binds the listener, and only then starts background workers. SIGINT or SIGTERM marks readiness as draining, shuts down HTTP work, drains workers, and closes lifecycle-owned adapters.
Execute blocks until the command or server lifecycle finishes. Return its error from main or log it as a fatal startup/runtime failure.

symbols.name: HookContext
symbols.summary: Read the request and values available to a collection or global hook.

parameters.name: Context
parameters.description:
Context carries cancellation, deadlines, and the active transaction.
Pass it to Local calls that must succeed or roll back with this operation.

parameters.name: Operation
parameters.description:
Operation names the document operation, such as Create, Update, or Read,
not the hook phase. Shared hooks should check it before running write-only work.

parameters.name: CollectionID
parameters.description:
CollectionID is the collection's stable resource ID, not its slug.
It is empty for a global operation.

parameters.name: GlobalID
parameters.description:
GlobalID is the global's stable resource ID, not its slug.
It is empty for a collection operation.

parameters.name: Actor
parameters.description: Actor is the authenticated document, or nil for an anonymous operation.

parameters.name: ActorCollection
parameters.description: ActorCollection identifies the exact auth collection that owns Actor.

parameters.name: Data
parameters.description:
Data contains values at this phase: submitted input in BeforeValidate,
then the completed document in BeforeChange and BeforeOperation on writes.
Change map entries to change stored values; assigning a new map to Data
does not replace the engine's values. Changes after saving are not persisted.

parameters.name: Document
parameters.description:
Document is the response document when available. AfterRead receives each
document in a list separately. Changes to Document.Values affect the response,
not stored data, and remain subject to field read access rules.

parameters.name: Original
parameters.description:
Original is a detached copy of the saved document before an update, delete,
or duplication. Changing it does not change storage.

parameters.name: Local
parameters.description:
Local performs nested reads and writes through the normal operation engine.
Pass Context to reuse the transaction, and pass Actor, ActorCollection, and
locale options explicitly when the nested operation represents the same user.
Standalone reads reject nested writes; AfterCommit starts new transactions.

parameters.name: Error
parameters.description:
Error is set only for after-error hooks and preserves the original failure.
Returning nil from AfterError does not make the failed operation succeed.

parameters.name: Locale
parameters.description:
Locale is the selected content language. Write hooks use the write locale;
AfterRead uses the response locale, whose values may include fallback text.

parameters.name: AllLocales
parameters.description:
AllLocales reports whether localized values contain maps keyed by locale.
It describes this hook's values, which may differ from the requested response.

symbols.name: Hook
symbols.summary: Run code during a collection or global lifecycle phase.

parameters.name: ctx
parameters.description: The operation, user, values, and local API for this phase. Change Data entries before saving or Document.Values to change the response.

returns.description: Before commit, an error fails and rolls back the operation. AfterCommit errors report a committed failure.

details: Return nil to continue or an error to stop. A pre-commit error rolls back the operation; an AfterCommit error cannot undo saved data.

symbols.name: CollectionHooks
symbols.summary: Register callbacks for collection or global reads, writes, and other lifecycle events.

parameters.name: BeforeDuplicate
parameters.description: BeforeDuplicate runs after the source is access-checked and copied but before validation.

parameters.name: BeforeValidate
parameters.description:
BeforeValidate runs before field hooks and built-in checks. On updates,
Data may contain only the submitted fields. This shared phase also runs for
reads and deletes; check Operation when changing write input.

parameters.name: BeforeChange
BeforeOperation
parameters.description:
BeforeOperation runs before the store operation, including reads and deletes.
On writes it follows BeforeChange; changed values are validated before saving.

parameters.name: BeforeRead
parameters.description: BeforeRead runs before one or many documents are read.

parameters.name: BeforeDelete
parameters.description: BeforeDelete runs after the original document is loaded but before deletion.

parameters.name: AfterChange
parameters.description:
AfterChange runs after create, duplicate, update, publish, or unpublish has
saved the document, but before commit. Returning an error rolls back the save.

parameters.name: AfterRead
parameters.description:
AfterRead runs for each response document, including mutation responses,
after computed fields resolve and before field read access removes values.

parameters.name: AfterDelete
parameters.description: AfterDelete runs inside the transaction after deletion or trashing.

parameters.name: AfterOperation
parameters.description:
AfterOperation runs after the store operation, including reads and deletes,
but before response processing and commit. Errors can still roll back writes.

parameters.name: AfterError
parameters.description:
AfterError observes a failure in this resource through Error. It cannot
suppress that failure; its own error is added to the returned error.

parameters.name: AfterCommit

symbols.summary: Choose how hooks run after their transaction commits.

parameters.name: Dispatch
parameters.description: Deliver one effect after its transaction commits.

returns.description: A delivery error that cannot roll back committed content.

details: Without a custom dispatcher, AfterCommit hooks run synchronously. A dispatcher must call effect.Run or arrange for it to run; a Go callback is not itself a durable task.

symbols.name: AfterCommitEffect

parameters.name: DocumentID

symbols.name: LocalizationConfig
symbols.summary: Content locales, fallback behavior, and optional request-scoped admin availability.

parameters.name: DefaultLocale
parameters.description: Locale selected when a request does not specify one.

parameters.name: DisableFallback
parameters.description: Requires exact locale values instead of following fallback chains.

parameters.name: AvailableLocales
parameters.description: Optionally reduces locales visible to one admin request without weakening API validation or authorization.

details: Leave Locales empty to disable content localization. When localization is enabled, DefaultLocale must name one configured locale and every fallback must also be configured.

FallbackLocales are checked in order after the requested locale unless DisableFallback is true. AvailableLocales only narrows the locale picker for the current admin request; it cannot add locales, change API validation, or grant access, and executable callbacks are never serialized into the schema manifest.
Assign this value to Config.Localization. Because the root package aliases the canonical core contract, an AvailableLocales callback names its input as core.LocaleAvailabilityContext.

symbols.name: Locale
symbols.summary: One content locale and its ordered fallback chain.

parameters.name: Code
parameters.description: Stable locale code used by APIs and storage.

parameters.name: FallbackLocales
parameters.description: Configured locale codes checked in order when this locale has no value.

details: Code is the stable wire and storage identity; changing it is a data migration. Label and RTL affect authoring presentation. Fallback chains must be acyclic and may name only configured locales.

symbols.summary: Validation, privacy, and image-variant policy for an upload collection.

parameters.name: MaxFileSize
parameters.description: Accepted byte limit; zero uses the framework default and values above 256 MiB are rejected.

parameters.name: MimeTypes

symbols.name: VersionConfig
symbols.summary: Drafts, snapshot retention, and autosave policy.

parameters.name: MaxPerDocument
parameters.description: Limits retained revisions; zero uses the framework default.

parameters.name: AutosaveInterval
parameters.description: Controls draft autosave frequency; zero resolves to the 30-second framework default.

details: Versions must be enabled on the collection/global. MaxPerDocument zero resolves to 100. AutosaveInterval zero currently resolves to 30 seconds, and a configured interval must be at least one second; it drives admin update calls rather than a server-side mutation timer. Optimistic revision checks are available through MutationOptions.

symbols.name: HandlerOptions

parameters.name: AdminAssets
parameters.description: Overrides the framework’s embedded admin asset filesystem.

parameters.name: MaxBodyBytes
parameters.description: Limits decoded request bodies; zero uses the framework default.

parameters.name: SecureCookies
parameters.description: Restricts authentication cookies to HTTPS requests.

parameters.name: AllowedOrigins
parameters.description: Lists browser origins permitted by credentialed CORS.

parameters.name: AllowedRequestHeaders
parameters.description: Appends application-owned CORS request headers; invalid HTTP token names are ignored.

parameters.name: AllowedHosts
parameters.description: Restricts Host to exact hostnames with optional ports; empty accepts syntactically valid development hosts.

parameters.name: TrustedProxyCIDRs
parameters.description: Lists proxies whose forwarded client addresses may be trusted.

parameters.name: AuthRateLimit
parameters.description: Sets maximum auth attempts per identity and client window.

parameters.name: Observe
parameters.description: Receives timing and status metadata for completed requests.

parameters.name: RequestError
parameters.description: Receives trusted diagnostic detail while public responses remain redacted.

parameters.name: RequestTimeout
parameters.description: Limits request execution; zero uses the default and a negative value disables the bound.

parameters.name: ReadinessTimeout
parameters.description: Bounds the complete readiness probe; zero uses five seconds and a negative value disables it.

parameters.name: DisableContentSecurityPolicy
parameters.description: Disables CSP when an upstream gateway owns it.

parameters.name: StrictTransportSecurity
parameters.description: Emits the configured HSTS value when every public request is HTTPS.

parameters.name: TaskBatch
parameters.description: Limits leases claimed during one polling cycle.

parameters.name: TaskQueues
parameters.description: Restricts this process to named worker queues; empty consumes every queue.

parameters.name: TaskLeaseDuration
parameters.description: Sets the lease extended while a handler runs.

parameters.name: TaskHeartbeatInterval
parameters.description: Sets heartbeat cadence and must be shorter than the lease.

parameters.name: TaskPruneBatch
parameters.description: Bounds expired terminal task records removed per cycle.

parameters.name: AuthPruneBatch
parameters.description: Bounds expired sessions and API keys removed per maintenance cycle.

parameters.name: JobError
parameters.description: Receives failures from scheduled background work.

details: Pass this value to App.Handler when embedding Ridu, or install it with WithHandlerOptions when Execute owns the server.

The zero value is development-friendly. Before production, set SecureCookies and AllowedHosts, add AllowedOrigins only for cross-origin browser clients, and trust only proxy ranges you operate. Body, request, readiness, worker, and maintenance bounds resolve independently when left at zero.

symbols.name: WithStore
symbols.summary: Provide the singular document-store adapter through the Execute lifecycle.

parameters.name: factory
parameters.description: A lazy constructor invoked once when Execute starts the HTTP server.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: WithStore is required only for the no-argument server branch of Execute. Project commands such as generate and check resolve config without applying this option, so they do not need DATABASE_URL or a reachable database.
The factory receives the server lifecycle context. Return an unopened error rather than terminating the process inside the factory; Execute wraps it as open document store and returns it to main.

The returned store must implement the base store.Store contract and every optional capability enabled by the application. Production startup also requires store.ReadinessStore unless ServerOptions.AllowUnverifiableReadiness delegates readiness checking to an external system.

Execute owns the returned adapter. On startup failure or shutdown it calls Close() or Close() error when implemented, bounded by ServerOptions.ShutdownTimeout. Optional upload storage closes first, then the document store.

symbols.name: WithProjectMigrations
symbols.summary: Register the selected adapter’s compiled migration driver for project commands.

parameters.name: driver
parameters.description: Compiled callback registry and adapter-owned project migration runner.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: The driver is used only by project migration commands whose artifacts contain compiled data callbacks. It is not used by schema generation or the ordinary HTTP runtime.
symbols.example: ridu.WithProjectMigrations(sqlite.ProjectMigrations(transforms...))

symbols.name: WithAddress
symbols.summary: Configure the HTTP listen address independently from the store adapter.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: A Go net.Listen TCP address such as :8080 or 127.0.0.1:8080.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: The default is :8080, which listens on every interface. Use a loopback address when Ridu must be reachable only through a local reverse proxy or during development.
This controls only the listener. Public host validation belongs to HandlerOptions.AllowedHosts.
symbols.example: ridu.WithAddress("127.0.0.1:8080")

symbols.name: WithUploadStorage
symbols.summary: Provide object storage through the Execute lifecycle.

parameters.name: factory
parameters.description: A lazy object-storage constructor invoked during server startup.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: The factory runs only in the server branch. It supplies Config.Storage before application construction, keeping credentials and network setup out of the resolved schema manifest.
Upload-enabled config still needs a stable Config.StorageNamespace and a document store with the upload capability contracts. Closable object storage shuts down before the document store.

symbols.name: WithHandlerOptions
symbols.summary: Configure the generated HTTP handler used by Execute.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: HTTP security, limits, admin assets, observers, readiness, and worker settings.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: Generated projects use this option to attach the compiled admin assets and environment-derived HTTP policy. Passing it replaces the complete HandlerOptions value; combine settings in one value rather than scattering repeated WithHandlerOptions calls.

symbols.name: WithServerOptions
symbols.summary: Configure production socket and graceful-drain bounds.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Socket, readiness admission, shutdown, and worker-drain settings.

returns.description: An option to pass directly to ridu.Execute.

details: Zero values select bounded production defaults. Repeating WithServerOptions replaces the complete value, so configure related bounds together.

symbols.name: NewTask
symbols.summary: Define a compiled typed durable task.
symbols.signature: func NewTask[Input, Output any](slug string, handler TaskHandler[Input, Output], options ...TaskOption) TypedTask[Input, Output]
details: Add the returned definition to Config.Tasks. Input and output use strict JSON contracts, are capped by MaxTaskPayloadBytes, and never select executable code from serialized data. The backing store must implement store.TaskStore.

symbols.name: TypedTask
symbols.summary: A registered typed handle for durable admission, status, and cancellation.
symbols.signature: type TypedTask[Input, Output any] = core.TypedTask[Input, Output]

parameters.name: TaskSlug
parameters.description: Returns the stable registered task slug.

parameters.name: Enqueue
parameters.description: Validates and durably admits typed input.

parameters.name: Result
parameters.description: Loads and decodes typed task status and output.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: Prevents queued work and fences a running attempt.

details: Only NewTask constructs a valid definition. Add it to Config.Tasks before using its runtime methods.
The handle slug/type contract must match the definition registered in the running application. HasOutput distinguishes a valid zero/null output from incomplete work.

symbols.name: TaskQueue
symbols.summary: Select the queue used by a typed task.

symbols.name: TaskRetries
symbols.summary: Persist retry count, delay, maximum delay, and backoff policy.
symbols.signature: func TaskRetries(maxAttempts int, delay, maxDelay time.Duration, backoff TaskBackoff) TaskOption
details: Persisted policy prevents deployments from silently changing already-admitted work.

symbols.name: TaskTimeout
symbols.summary: Bound one handler attempt.

symbols.name: TaskRetention
symbols.summary: Keep terminal task status/output for a bounded duration.

symbols.name: TaskAdmissionReconciler
symbols.summary: Repair durable domain records that missed task admission.
details: The runtime invokes this bounded, idempotent callback before each selected claim cycle, including startup.

symbols.name: RetryTask
symbols.summary: Return a retryable handler failure using configured backoff.
symbols.signature: func RetryTask(code string, cause error) error

symbols.name: RetryTaskAfter
symbols.summary: Return a retryable handler failure with an explicit delay.
symbols.signature: func RetryTaskAfter(code string, cause error, delay time.Duration) error

symbols.name: AbortTask
symbols.summary: Return a terminal handler failure.
symbols.signature: func AbortTask(code string, cause error) error
details: Use stable non-secret codes. Local runtime, store, and codec boundary failures use structured TaskError values. Handler panics and handler/output failures are classified into durable retry or dead-letter state instead.

symbols.name: CollectionHooks
symbols.summary: CollectionHooks configures resource-level callbacks through Collection.Hooks or Global.Hooks. Use BeforeChange to change values before a save, AfterRead to change a response without changing storage, and AfterCommit for effects that must run only after a successful commit. Each list runs in declaration order. Resource hooks run before field hooks in the same phase, except AfterCommit, where field hooks run first. Globals do not support BeforeDuplicate, BeforeDelete, or AfterDelete.

parameters.name: BeforeDuplicate
parameters.description: BeforeDuplicate runs after the source is access-checked and copied but before validation.

parameters.name: BeforeValidate
parameters.description:
BeforeValidate runs before field hooks and built-in checks. On updates,
Data may contain only the submitted fields. This shared phase also runs for
reads and deletes; check Operation when changing write input.

parameters.name: BeforeChange
BeforeOperation
parameters.description:
BeforeOperation runs before the store operation, including reads and deletes.
On writes it follows BeforeChange; changed values are validated before saving.

parameters.name: BeforeRead
parameters.description: BeforeRead runs before one or many documents are read.

parameters.name: BeforeDelete
parameters.description: BeforeDelete runs after the original document is loaded but before deletion.

parameters.name: AfterChange
parameters.description:
AfterChange runs after create, duplicate, update, publish, or unpublish has
saved the document, but before commit. Returning an error rolls back the save.

parameters.name: AfterRead
parameters.description:
AfterRead runs for each response document, including mutation responses,
after computed fields resolve and before field read access removes values.

parameters.name: AfterDelete
parameters.description: AfterDelete runs inside the transaction after deletion or trashing.

parameters.name: AfterOperation
parameters.description:
AfterOperation runs after the store operation, including reads and deletes,
but before response processing and commit. Errors can still roll back writes.

parameters.name: AfterError
parameters.description:
AfterError observes a failure in this resource through Error. It cannot
suppress that failure; its own error is added to the returned error.

parameters.description:
GlobalID is the global's stable resource ID, not its slug.
It is empty for a collection operation.

parameters.name: Actor
parameters.description: Actor is the authenticated document, or nil for an anonymous operation.

parameters.name: ActorCollection
parameters.description: ActorCollection identifies the exact auth collection that owns Actor.

parameters.name: Data
parameters.description:
Data contains values at this phase: submitted input in BeforeValidate,
then the completed document in BeforeChange and BeforeOperation on writes.
Change map entries to change stored values; assigning a new map to Data
does not replace the engine's values. Changes after saving are not persisted.

parameters.name: Document
parameters.description:
Document is the response document when available. AfterRead receives each
document in a list separately. Changes to Document.Values affect the response,
not stored data, and remain subject to field read access rules.

parameters.name: Original
parameters.description:
Original is a detached copy of the saved document before an update, delete,
or duplication. Changing it does not change storage.

parameters.name: Local
parameters.description:
Local performs nested reads and writes through the normal operation engine.
Pass Context to reuse the transaction, and pass Actor, ActorCollection, and
locale options explicitly when the nested operation represents the same user.
Standalone reads reject nested writes; AfterCommit starts new transactions.

parameters.name: Error
parameters.description:
Error is set only for after-error hooks and preserves the original failure.
Returning nil from AfterError does not make the failed operation succeed.

parameters.name: Locale
parameters.description:
Locale is the selected content language. Write hooks use the write locale;
AfterRead uses the response locale, whose values may include fallback text.

parameters.name: AllLocales
parameters.description:
AllLocales reports whether localized values contain maps keyed by locale.
It describes this hook's values, which may differ from the requested response.

symbols.name: Access
symbols.summary: Access configures who may create, read, or update a field value. Assign it with a concrete field's Access method; an omitted rule leaves that operation unrestricted. Access replaces the field's complete policy group, while RestrictAccess adds only the supplied rules and requires both old and new rules to allow the operation.

symbols.name: AccessRule
symbols.summary: AccessRule decides whether one field value may be created, read, or updated. Return false during a write to reject the operation, or during a read to omit the field from the response. Returning an error stops the operation. Field rules cannot return the query predicates supported by collection access rules.

symbols.name: Admin
symbols.summary: Admin configures how a field is presented and edited in the framework admin. It never grants API access or changes storage behavior; use Access for authorization. A field's Admin method replaces the complete group, while EditAdmin preserves members its callback does not change. Ridu snapshots maps on input and output so retained drafts cannot mutate a published field.

symbols.summary: Configure the header for ordinary Blocks and rich-text blocks.

parameters.name: NameField
parameters.description: Optional name of a direct stored Text child to edit in the block header. Slug fields, nested paths and custom field editors are rejected. Leave unset to keep the existing content summary.

parameters.description: Direct stored scalar child used as the content summary. With NameField configured, this becomes the empty name input’s placeholder; an unavailable summary falls back to the untitled block label.

details: Declare the name field explicitly in the block’s Fields. The header replaces its body placement while retaining ordinary validation, access, visibility, localization and hooks. The name stays separate from the published heading.

Rich-text cards use the same header input, with undo/redo support. Editing drawers include the name in their detached draft: Apply commits it with the other fields and Cancel discards it.

symbols.name: DefaultFunc
symbols.summary: DefaultFunc supplies a server-side initial value for an eligible omitted field. Root and Siblings are snapshots at initialization; Prior is the persisted enclosing object or stable row (empty for new rows). ID may be empty. symbols.summary: Hooks registers transforms and event callbacks for one field. Each list runs in declaration order for each field occurrence, including nested array rows. parameters.name: BeforeDuplicate
parameters.description:
BeforeDuplicate receives raw copied input before validation. It runs only
when duplicating a collection document, after the resource hook.

parameters.name: BeforeValidate
parameters.description:
BeforeValidate receives raw input before built-in validation. It can supply
or normalize a value before conversion to T. This shared phase also runs on
reads and deletes; check the context's Operation for write-only logic.

parameters.name: BeforeChange
parameters.description:
BeforeChange transforms T after initial built-in checks on create,
duplicate, update, publish, and unpublish. Custom validators run later.

parameters.name: BeforeOperation
parameters.description:
BeforeOperation transforms T before the store operation, after BeforeChange
on writes. This shared phase also runs on reads and deletes.

parameters.name: BeforeDelete
parameters.description: BeforeDelete observes the saved value before trashing or permanent deletion.

parameters.name: AfterChange
parameters.description:
AfterChange observes a saved create, duplicate, update, publish, or unpublish
before commit. It cannot replace the field; an error rolls back the save.

parameters.name: AfterDelete
parameters.description:
AfterDelete observes a value after trashing or permanent deletion but before
commit. An error can still roll back the deletion.

parameters.name: AfterOperation
parameters.description:
AfterOperation observes the result before response processing and commit.
It also runs on reads and deletes; check Operation for write-only work.

parameters.name: AfterCommit
parameters.description:
AfterCommit observes the value outside the committed transaction, before
resource AfterCommit hooks. It also runs for reads. Errors cannot roll back
saved data, and later effects still run.

symbols.name: LiveValidator
symbols.summary: Check an unsaved field value on the server and return feedback before the author saves.
symbols.signature: type LiveValidator[T any] func(operation.LiveValidationContext, operation.Value[T]) ([]operation.Issue, error)

parameters.name: ctx
parameters.description: The request, user, exact locale, readable form values, saved values, and a read-only document reader.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The current typed value after retaining omitted update fields. Get returns the value and whether it is present. Missing and null values are empty; use ctx.Input.Lookup to distinguish omitted input from an explicit null.

returns.description: Return nil, nil when the check finds no problem; issues, nil for messages the author can act on; or an error when the check could not run. An error fails the feedback request. An issue with no Target belongs to the current field.

details: Register this callback with LiveValidate. Register save rules separately with Validate: live feedback does not run during Save and cannot guarantee that a later save will succeed.

T matches the field’s write type: string for text-like fields and single choices; float64 for Number; bool for Checkbox; []string for MultiSelect; operation.ID or []operation.ID for relationships and uploads; store.Value for structured and plugin fields.

Ridu skips a callback when the field value cannot be decoded to its expected type. Missing or null input can still reach a callback as an empty operation.Value. Structured store.Value callbacks must check child values themselves; defaults, save hooks, and full validation have not run.
Keep the check repeatable and free of writes or other side effects. Pass ctx.Context to cancellable work and ctx.Local.FindByID; the request has a five-second deadline.

The interface is sealed so Ridu can snapshot every supported field safely.

symbols.summary: Read the configured dynamic default without running it.

returns.description: The configured callback, or nil if this field has a literal default or no default. Check for nil before calling it in a test.

symbols.name: NumberField.DefaultFrom
symbols.summary: Use a callback to choose the initial number when this field is omitted.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: A non-nil function that receives operation.DefaultContext and returns an operation.Value[float64] plus an error. Return Present(value) to supply a value, Empty to supply no default, or an error to stop the operation.

returns.description: A new NumberField with this callback as its only default. The original field is unchanged; this replaces any previous Default or DefaultFrom setting.

details: The callback runs on the server when omitted input is eligible for initialization. It does not prefill an unsaved form or refill a field on every edit. See the default values guide for new objects, repeated rows, and locales.
The returned number must still pass configured bounds and other validation.

symbols.name: NumberList
symbols.summary: Add a field containing an ordered list of numbers.

returns.description: A NumberListField definition. Call its methods to set item limits, list length, defaults, or callbacks.

details: Order and duplicates are preserved. Items must be finite numbers; numeric strings are rejected. Min and Max apply to each number, including both bounds.
Required requires at least one item. MinRows and MaxRows count items; they do not limit each item’s value. An explicit empty list remains an empty array.
Validators and hooks receive the complete []float64 value. Use Array for items with child fields, or MultiSelect for choices from a predefined set.
symbols.example: field.NumberList("availableSizes").Min(0).MaxRows(20)

symbols.name: NumberListField
symbols.summary: A configurable list of numbers.
details: Create it with field.NumberList(name). Setters return a new definition, leaving the original unchanged.
List-length limits use MinRows and MaxRows. Numeric bounds apply to each number.
Callbacks operate on the whole []float64 list. Items have no child field definitions or saved row keys.

symbols.name: OutputTransform
symbols.summary: OutputTransform changes one field in the response without changing storage. Its context supplies response values, which may include related documents and locale fallback. Return Keep or Replace, as for a write transform. Field read access still runs afterward; visible context data is not permission to expose it. AfterRead runs after resource response hooks on reads and mutation responses, before final field redaction. Registration determines the callback phase. An error stops the response and can roll back an uncommitted mutation.

symbols.name: RawTransform
symbols.summary: RawTransform checks or changes one field before input is converted to its Go type. The context supplies surrounding values; the separate value is this field's raw input and may be invalid. Empty means omitted; Present(store.Null()) means explicit null. Return Keep to leave it unchanged, Replace to change this field, or an error to stop. Changing a context snapshot does not change the document.

symbols.summary: Reference is an immutable field selector. Its dot-separated path names stored fields through non-repeated groups or named tabs, excluding presentation wrappers and repeated row selectors. Each use resolves in its own field scope.

symbols.name: Reference.Err
symbols.summary: Err checks path structure. Configuration resolution checks target existence and rejects paths that cross repeated fields or end at incompatible values.

symbols.name: Reference.IsZero

symbols.name: Reference.MarshalJSON
symbols.summary: MarshalJSON retains the authored scope and path.

symbols.name: Reference.Path

symbols.name: TextList
symbols.summary: Add a field containing an ordered list of text values.

returns.description: A TextListField definition. Call its methods to set item limits, list length, defaults, or callbacks.

details: Order and duplicates are preserved. Strings are not trimmed. MinLength and MaxLength apply to each string, counting Unicode code points.
Required requires at least one item. MinRows and MaxRows count items; they do not limit each item’s value. An explicit empty list remains an empty array.
Validators and hooks receive the complete []string value. Use Array for items with child fields, or MultiSelect for choices from a predefined set.
symbols.example: field.TextList("sellingPoints").MinRows(1).MaxRows(8).MaxLength(120)

symbols.name: TextListField
symbols.summary: A configurable list of strings.
details: Create it with field.TextList(name). Setters return a new definition, leaving the original unchanged.
List-length limits use MinRows and MaxRows. Text-length limits apply to each string.
Callbacks operate on the whole []string list. Items have no child field definitions or saved row keys.

symbols.name: Validator
symbols.summary: Validator checks a field before saving, after built-in checks and write hooks. Root and Siblings include retained values and earlier write transformations; Prior remains the persisted enclosing object or row. LiveValidationContext instead describes sparse input before defaults and save transformations. Return issues for values the author needs to fix, or an error if the check could not run. An issue belongs to this field unless its Target names a child.

parameters.name: MaxUploadLockConnections
parameters.description:
MaxUploadLockConnections bounds the separate advisory-lock pool used
while object storage and document transactions are coordinated. Keeping
this pool separate prevents staged uploads from starving their own
document transactions. Zero selects four connections.

details: Zero values select bounded Ridu defaults. Negative duration values explicitly disable the corresponding timeout.

AllowInsecureTransport is for local sockets or externally secured development transport; keep it false in production. The upload lock pool defaults to four connections and stays separate so staged uploads cannot starve their own document transactions.

parameters.name: AllowInsecureDatabase
parameters.description:
AllowInsecureDatabase explicitly permits a PostgreSQL connection that can
fall back to plaintext. It is intended only for local migration drills.

parameters.name: AllowMaintenance
parameters.description:
AllowMaintenance admits traffic-sensitive semantic steps such as content
rewrites, compiled data transforms, resource retirement, and
reference-index rebuilds. Every old writer must be stopped while they run.
It does not relax artifact validation.

parameters.name: AllowUnbounded
parameters.description:
AllowUnbounded permits a zero operational timeout. Without this explicit
admission, zero selects the runner's bounded production default.

parameters.name: AdvisoryLockWait
parameters.description: AdvisoryLockWait bounds how long this runner waits for another migrator.

parameters.name: LockTimeout
parameters.description: LockTimeout bounds PostgreSQL lock acquisition inside a phase.

parameters.name: StatementTimeout
parameters.description: StatementTimeout bounds one transactional SQL statement.

parameters.name: BatchTimeout
parameters.description: BatchTimeout bounds the complete execution of one checkpoint batch.

parameters.name: ConcurrentIndexTimeout
parameters.description: ConcurrentIndexTimeout bounds one CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY command.

parameters.name: IdleInTransactionTimeout
parameters.description: IdleInTransactionTimeout protects a paused transactional phase.

parameters.name: StopAfterPhase
parameters.description:
StopAfterPhase and StopAfterStep are explicit, successfully committed
rollout boundaries. A transaction phase can stop only at its final step.

symbols.summary: Bounded connection behavior for the embedded SQLite store.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Path is a filesystem path, a file: SQLite URI, or :memory:.

parameters.name: BusyTimeout
parameters.description:
BusyTimeout bounds how long SQLite waits for another writer. Zero selects
ten seconds. Negative values and values above SQLite's signed 32-bit
millisecond limit are rejected.

parameters.name: DisableWAL
parameters.description:
DisableWAL keeps file databases in their existing journal mode. WAL is
enabled by default because it permits readers while the single writer is
active. SQLite memory databases ignore WAL mode.

parameters.name: MaxConnections
parameters.description:
MaxConnections bounds pooled readers. Operation transactions still use
BEGIN IMMEDIATE and SQLite's single-writer contract.

details: Zero values select safe local defaults. File databases enable WAL unless DisableWAL is set; SQLite still has one writer.

modules.name: mongodb
modules.summary: The official replica-set MongoDB store, additive development index synchronization, and immutable forward-only migration lifecycle.

symbols.name: Open
symbols.summary: Open a verified-TLS MongoDB replica-set database with bounded defaults.
symbols.signature: func Open(ctx context.Context, databaseURL string) (*Store, error)
details: The URL must select one database. Open checks for a writable replica-set primary with logical sessions but does not create collections, indexes, or migration state.

symbols.summary: Open the store with explicit transport, timeout, application-name, and pool bounds.
symbols.signature: func OpenWithConfig(ctx context.Context, config Config) (*Store, error)

symbols.name: Config
symbols.summary: Runtime-only MongoDB connection behavior.

parameters.name: DatabaseURL
parameters.description: Credential-bearing URL selecting the application database.

parameters.name: AllowInsecureTransport
parameters.description: Allow an insecure local development connection; keep false in production.

parameters.name: ApplicationName
parameters.description: Client application name; defaults to ridu.

parameters.name: ConnectTimeout
parameters.description: Connection bound; zero selects the Ridu default.

parameters.name: ServerSelectionTimeout
parameters.description: Primary-selection bound; zero selects the Ridu default.

parameters.name: MaxConnectionIdleTime
parameters.description: Pooled idle-time bound; zero selects the Ridu default.

parameters.name: MaxPoolSize
parameters.description: Maximum pool size; zero selects ten.

parameters.name: MinPoolSize
parameters.description: Minimum pool size; cannot exceed MaxPoolSize.

details: DatabaseURL never belongs in manifests, artifacts, generated contracts, or diagnostics. Negative durations and invalid pool bounds are rejected.

symbols.name: Store
symbols.summary: A replica-set implementation of Ridu’s document, snapshot, auth, preference, task, lock, upload, readiness, and migration contracts.
symbols.signature:
type Store struct {
	client   *mongo.Client
	database *mongo.Database
	now      func() time.Time

	closeMu  sync.Mutex
	closed   bool
	closeErr error

	indexLifecycleMu            sync.Mutex
	indexesMu                   sync.RWMutex
	verifiedIndexes             map[schema.StableID]mongoVerifiedIndexPlan
	verifiedVersionIndexes      map[schema.StableID]bool
	verifiedReferenceIndexes    bool
	verifiedPreferenceIndexes   bool
	verifiedDocumentLockIndexes bool
	verifiedTaskIndexes         bool
	verifiedAuthIndexes         bool
	verifiedUploadLockIndexes   bool

	uploadLockRetry time.Duration
	uploadLockWait  time.Duration

	uploadLockLifecycleMu     sync.Mutex
	uploadLockLifecycleCtx    context.Context
	uploadLockLifecycleCancel context.CancelFunc
	uploadLockOperations      sync.WaitGroup
}

parameters.name: store.MigrationReadinessStore
parameters.description: Checks the complete ledger against the release-binary fingerprint.

parameters.name: store.AuthStore
parameters.description: Persists credentials, sessions, tokens, API keys, and rate limits.

parameters.name: store.AuthMaintenanceStore
parameters.description: Prunes expired auth records in bounded batches.

parameters.name: store.UploadObjectLocker
parameters.description: Coordinates upload object changes across processes.

details: Use the application and Local API for content operations; the adapter exposes no raw BSON filter, database handle, ObjectID contract, or second Mongo-specific content API.
Transactions add auth/bootstrap/unlock, versions, distinct, windows, upload-reference lookup, and transaction-level upload locking to store.Transaction.

Production support is limited to generated starter and blank applications on Linux x86-64 with MongoDB Community 8.2.9, SCRAM-SHA-256, verified TLS, and a writable three-member replica set. Atlas, DocumentDB, Cosmos DB, standalone or sharded deployments, and other versions, topologies, and platforms are not supported.

type RunnerOptions struct {

parameters.name: AllowMaintenance
parameters.description: Admit pending traffic-sensitive live steps after writers drain, or complete semantic shadow replay.

parameters.name: AllowUnbounded
parameters.description: Explicitly permit a zero wait or operation timeout.

parameters.name: LeaseWait
parameters.description: Maximum wait for the single-migrator fenced lease.

parameters.name: LeaseDuration
parameters.description: Renewable bounded lease duration used for crash recovery.

details: Zero values select bounded defaults unless AllowUnbounded explicitly admits an unbounded wait or operation; lease expiry remains bounded.

symbols.name: AdminPlugin
symbols.summary: A Go plugin’s exported collection of admin field editors, pages, and other components.

parameters.name: apiVersion
parameters.description: Added by `defineAdminPlugin` from the versioned import. Do not set this yourself.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Required. Match the Go plugin’s Key(), for example color or editorial-tools. Use a lowercase key with hyphens between words.

parameters.name: pairingVersion
parameters.description: Required positive integer. Match `Admin.PairingVersion` in the Go descriptor. Increase it when an older Go or admin package would no longer work with the other.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.type: Readonly<Record<string, RegisteredPluginField & { readonly type: "plugin"; readonly fieldType?: never; }>>
parameters.description: Optional. Map Go field-type keys to `definePluginField` results. These become the default editors for those new field types; the keys match `PluginFieldType.Key` in Go.

parameters.name: components
parameters.type: Readonly<Record<string, RegisteredPluginField & ({ readonly type: Exclude<FieldType, "plugin">; } | { readonly type: "plugin"; readonly fieldType: string; })>>
parameters.description: Optional. Map component names to `defineFieldComponent` results. Go chooses an alternative editor with `field.PluginComponent(pluginKey, componentName)`.

parameters.name: rowLabels
parameters.description: Optional. Row headings made with `defineRowLabelPlugin`. Go selects them with `field.PluginComponent` in `Admin.RowLabel`.

parameters.name: messages
parameters.description: Optional. Translations bundled with the plugin, created with `defineAdminMessages`.

parameters.name: assets
parameters.description: Optional. Package-relative modules or styles imported during the admin build. Keep the list and order identical to `Admin.Assets` in the Go descriptor.

parameters.name: routes
parameters.description: Optional. Add pages inside the admin, each with a relative path, component, and optional navigation link. Plugin routes must also appear in the Go descriptor.

parameters.name: dashboard
parameters.description: Optional. Add panels before or after the dashboard, or replace it. Each entry names a key, component, and position; the default position is after.

parameters.name: login
parameters.description: Optional. Add content before or after sign-in, or replace the screen. A replacement can render `defaultView` to retain the login form.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: Optional. Add content to or replace the profile or security screen, selected by surface.

parameters.name: navigation
parameters.description: Optional. Add content around the navigation links or replace navigation. Use routes for a new page with its own navigation link.

parameters.name: logoutButton
parameters.description: Optional. Replace the account menu’s sign-out control. The component receives `host.logout()` to end the session.

parameters.name: views
parameters.description: Optional. Wrap or replace collection lists, create/edit forms, global editors, or the not-found page. The component can render `defaultView` to keep the built-in screen.

parameters.name: branding
parameters.description: Optional. Replace the login logo, navigation logo, or account avatar. Each location accepts one replacement.

parameters.name: shell
parameters.description: Optional. Add a component to the header, global actions, or account settings menu.

parameters.name: providers
parameters.description: Optional. Share context between components by wrapping the admin. The first provider is outermost; every provider must render `defaultView`.

parameters.name: listCells
parameters.description: Optional. Change how a field appears in a collection table. Each entry selects a collection, field path, and component.

parameters.name: documentActions
parameters.description: Optional. Add buttons to saved collection documents. A component implements the action; an optional requires permission hides it when the user lacks that permission.

parameters.name: documentViews
parameters.description: Optional. Add tabs beside Edit and API on saved documents or globals. Each entry includes a key, label, and component; collection can limit where it appears.

details: Use the linked registration helper to create this value. Component arrays keep their order; installed plugin entries come before application entries. Each replacement location accepts one component.

parameters.name: definition
parameters.type: FieldDefinition<Value, Config, "plugin", Input> & { decodeConfig: (value: unknown) => Config; decodeInput: (value: unknown) => Input; }
parameters.description: Required object containing component and `decodeValue`. Add `decodeInput` for a different write shape, or `decodeConfig` for editor settings.

options.name: component
options.description: Required. The Svelte editor. It reads `field.value`, writes unsaved changes with `field.set(...)`, and receives config only when `decodeConfig` is supplied.

options.name: decodeValue
options.description: Required. Check a saved value and return the value type the component can read. Throw an Error for invalid data. Runs synchronously; Ridu handles null and undefined separately.

options.name: decodeInput
options.description: Optional. Check values passed to `field.set` when the server accepts a different shape from saved data. Defaults to `decodeValue` when omitted. It must return synchronously.

options.name: decodeConfig
options.description: Optional. Check Go field settings and return the component’s config prop. Without this decoder, the plugin’s field settings must be empty and the component receives no config prop.

returns.description: A frozen `PluginFieldRegistration` with type: "plugin", retaining inferred saved-value and input types. Put it under the Go field-type key in `defineAdminPlugin`({ fields: ... }). The helper does not create a Go field or register server validation.

details: Use this for a new type such as color.Field("accent"). The fields map key must match `PluginFieldType.Key` in the Go descriptor. Do not put app: on that key; app:name belongs to application field editors.

For a character counter or another input on an existing text, number, or checkbox field in one application, use `defineFieldEditor`. For a named alternative supplied by a plugin, use `defineFieldComponent`.

`Value` describes data returned by the server. `Input` describes data sent back and defaults to `Value`. `Config` is inferred from `decodeConfig`. TypeScript usually infers these from the decoder functions; explicit generic arguments are unnecessary.

When reading an unsaved form value, Ridu tries `decodeValue` first and then `decodeInput` if a separate input decoder is present. `field.value` may therefore contain either saved data or a pending edit.

Keep decoders synchronous and free of side effects. They may run on every read. Throw an Error with a useful message for unsupported data; `field.rawValue` remains available when a plugin needs to display or recover it.
Browser decoding does not replace the Go validator. `field.set(...)` changes the unsaved form; the document Save action sends it to the server for validation.
The example is the color plugin’s admin entry. Follow Build a field plugin for its complete Svelte editor, value decoder, and Go implementation.

parameters.description: Required object with type and component, plus `decodeConfig` only when the editor has settings supplied from Go.

options.name: type
options.description: Required. Match the Go field type: text, textarea, email, date, code, number, checkbox, text-list, or number-list. This determines the value your component reads and writes.

options.name: component
options.description: Required. A Svelte component receiving the matching FieldEditorProps. Use `field.value` for the current input and `field.set(...)` to change it.

A copy of the field's resolved settings, including its current path, label and rules.
`schema.admin.readOnly` reflects field configuration and access, not a pending document save.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description:
The latest value in the form, including unsaved edits. Objects and arrays are
copied: modifying this result does not update the form. Call `set` to change it.

`null` and `undefined` mean the field is empty or absent. Other values pass
through `decodeValue`, or through `decodeInput` if the output decoder rejects
a pending edit. Reading throws if neither decoder accepts the value.

parameters.name: rawValue
parameters.description:
A copy of the current value before decoding. Use this to display or recover
older data your decoder rejects; validate it before treating it as `Value`.

parameters.name: issues
parameters.description: Current form and server validation issues for this field and its children.

parameters.name: liveValidation
parameters.description: Read the check’s status or call retry() after a failure. Ridu runs the requests; messages appear alongside other validation issues in field.issues.

parameters.name: readOnly
parameters.description:
Whether changes are currently blocked, for example by access rules, a save in
progress, or a stale binding. Bindings from `form.bind` also respect the source
editor's read-only state. `set` checks this again when called.

parameters.name: stale
parameters.description: Whether this connection has expired. Once true, it cannot become usable again.

parameters.name: set
parameters.description:
Replace the value in the unsaved form. Use `null` to clear it; `undefined` is
rejected. Ridu copies and decodes the supplied value, checks editability, and
updates its normal form state. This does not send a save request to the server.

Throws if the binding is stale, the field is read-only, the decoder rejects the
value, or a structured edit changes a protected child field. Server validation
still runs when the document is saved.

details: Ridu creates and cleans up this field connection. For arrays and blocks, it follows the row’s stable _key through reorder. Removing the field or replacing the form makes the connection stale; use the binding supplied to the newly mounted editor.

symbols.name: PluginForm
symbols.summary: Read the containing document form, or connect to another field to update it.

parameters.name: bind
parameters.description:
Connect to another field in this document's unsaved form.

Paths start at the document root: `"title"`, `"seo.description"`, or
`"reviews.0.note"`. The last example selects the first review **now**. Keep
the returned binding: it follows that same row if the user reorders reviews.
Calling `bind("reviews.0.note")` later would select the row at index 0 then.

Create the binding before starting a request, timer or other delayed work.
Ridu disables it if the target disappears or the source editor closes, and
also when the document, locale, schema or saved/reset form values change.
Later reads and writes throw instead of editing a different field or document.
The target must be editable, and the source editor must be editable too.

The returned value type is `unknown`: a string path does not prove a field's
TypeScript type. Check read values and supply the target field's expected shape.
`bind` itself throws if the path has no identifiable field. Repeated rows
currently require nonempty, unique `_key` values.

parameters.name: contentLocale
parameters.description: The content locale being edited, such as `"fr"`; separate from the admin UI language.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: Which collection document or global is being edited, when supplied by this form.

parameters.name: get
parameters.description:
Read a copy of a value by its current document-root path, such as `"title"`
or `"reviews.0.note"`. Returns undefined for a missing value. A numbered path
reads whichever row is at that position now; it does not remember row identity.
Check the returned value's type before using it.

parameters.name: issuesFor
parameters.description: Current validation issues at or below a document-root path, including server issues.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.description:
Copy all current form values, including unsaved edits. The result is a snapshot:
it does not update when the user types, and changing it does not update the form.
This is form data, not a fresh document fetched from the server.

modules.name: ridu CLI
modules.summary: The implemented project lifecycle: scaffolding, generation, migrations, development, checks, builds, diagnostics, and static plugin management.

symbols.name: ridu new
symbols.summary: Scaffold a thin Ridu application, resolve Go dependencies, and generate its first contracts.
symbols.signature: ridu new [--template starter|blank] [--database postgres|sqlite|mongodb] [--package-manager npm|bun|pnpm|yarn] [--agent codex|claude|cursor|all|none] [--no-agent] [--module <go-module>] [--scope <npm-scope>] [directory]

parameters.name: --template
parameters.description: Embedded application template; defaults to starter.

parameters.name: --database
parameters.description: Official database adapter; defaults to postgres.

parameters.name: --package-manager
parameters.description: Frontend package manager; defaults to npm outside the interactive wizard.

parameters.name: --agent
parameters.description: Release-matched local coding-agent layout; defaults to codex outside a terminal.

parameters.name: --no-agent
parameters.description: Do not install coding-agent entrypoints, skills, or ownership manifest.

parameters.name: --module
parameters.description: Go module path; defaults to example.com/<project>.

parameters.name: --scope
parameters.description: npm scope for the generated admin workspace; defaults to @<project>.

parameters.name: directory
parameters.description: New project directory, which must not already exist.

details: The scaffold is kept if dependency setup or initial generation fails, and the CLI prints recovery commands.
--release-version is a framework-development override for exercising an alternate dependency release; ordinary application authors should not use it.
symbols.example:
ridu new --package-manager npm \
	--module github.com/acme/content \
	--scope @acme \
	content
cd content
npm install
npm run dev

symbols.name: ridu agent install
symbols.summary: Install a release-matched local agent layout into an existing Ridu project.
details: Installs both ridu-project and payload-to-ridu with their offline references. Existing AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md instructions are preserved, and unmanaged skill files are never replaced.
.ridu-agent-docs.json records only framework-owned files, digests, selected layouts, and the framework release.
symbols.example: ridu agent install --agent claude

symbols.name: ridu agent sync
symbols.summary: Synchronize installed framework-owned skill references with the current CLI release.
details: Sync validates every recorded digest before writing and stops if a managed file contains local edits. Root project instructions are never synchronized.

symbols.name: ridu doctor
symbols.summary: Diagnose Go, Bun, project discovery, frontend dependencies, and local database prerequisites.
details: Docker or OrbStack is optional when DATABASE_URL is already set for PostgreSQL or MongoDB, and is not required for SQLite projects. doctor validates RIDU_SQLITE_PATH when configured and reports whether frontend dependencies are installed or will be installed by dev/build.

symbols.name: ridu dev
symbols.summary: Run the selected database adapter, generation, safe schema sync, API, admin watch mode, and Go-config watching together.

parameters.name: --database-url
parameters.description: PostgreSQL or MongoDB development URL; defaults to DATABASE_URL, then the selected scaffold Compose service.

parameters.name: --database-path
parameters.description: SQLite-only development path; defaults to RIDU_SQLITE_PATH, then .ridu/development.sqlite.

parameters.name: --address
parameters.description: Go API listen address; defaults to 127.0.0.1:8080.

parameters.name: --no-docker
parameters.description: Do not start the scaffolded PostgreSQL or MongoDB Compose service.

parameters.name: --no-install
parameters.description: Do not install missing frontend dependencies with the configured package manager.

parameters.name: --no-sync
parameters.description: Do not apply a safe non-destructive development schema plan.

details: Automatic sync pauses instead of guessing when a possible rename needs review. Create and apply a migration, then restart dev.
Development injects local-only insecure cookie/database admissions into the child server; those are not production defaults.
symbols.example:
ridu dev --database-url "$DATABASE_URL" --no-docker
ridu dev --database-path .ridu/development.sqlite

symbols.name: ridu generate
symbols.summary: Resolve executable Go config and atomically write every configured generated contract.

parameters.name: --check
parameters.description: Compare expected bytes without writing; exit unsuccessfully on missing or stale output.

details: Generation executes the application’s versioned private manifest command; it never parses Go source and never connects to the database.
Configured outputs include the canonical schema manifest, Go and TypeScript contracts/client module, OpenAPI, and static admin plugin registry.
symbols.example:
ridu generate
git diff -- generated/
ridu generate --check

symbols.name: ridu check
symbols.summary: Run the generated-contract, migration-history, Go, TypeScript, and Svelte project checks.
details: The command checks generation drift, current migration history, gofmt, go vet, go test ./..., then the project Bun check script when an admin is configured. It does not silently regenerate stale contracts.

symbols.name: ridu build
symbols.summary: Regenerate contracts, build the admin, and atomically install one production Go binary.

parameters.name: --output
parameters.description: Binary path; defaults to dist/<project> (with .exe on Windows).

details: Missing frontend dependencies are installed first. The admin assets are compiled before go build -trimpath; the final binary is renamed into place only after a successful build.
symbols.example: ridu build --output ./bin/content

symbols.name: ridu migrate create
symbols.summary: Plan and write one reviewable immutable migration artifact without connecting to a database.

parameters.name: --accept-renames
parameters.description: PostgreSQL or MongoDB: accept every unambiguous detected rename without an interactive prompt.

parameters.name: --transform
parameters.description: SQLite or MongoDB: bind a named compiled data transform to the immutable artifact.

parameters.name: --allow-destructive
parameters.description: Record destructive changes confirmed by the selected adapter planner after explicit review.

details: PostgreSQL and MongoDB rename candidates require confirmation or --accept-renames. SQLite rejects --accept-renames and uses --transform instead for stored canonical JSON rewrites. MongoDB transforms run through the compiled project migration driver. Destructive approval does not bypass semantic transitions Ridu cannot safely automate.
symbols.example:
ridu migrate create --name rename-post-title
git diff -- migrations/

symbols.name: ridu migrate plan
symbols.summary: Inspect pending immutable execution topology without applying it.
details: PostgreSQL and MongoDB use --database-url or DATABASE_URL and accept --allow-insecure-database only for local development; SQLite uses --database-path or RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Current executable config must match the latest artifact target before database inspection proceeds. JSON output exposes adapter-owned phase, step, checksum, and state details.

symbols.name: ridu migrate status
symbols.summary: Compare immutable artifact history with the database ledger.
details: PostgreSQL and MongoDB use --database-url or DATABASE_URL; SQLite uses --database-path or RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Status is read-only and does not accept maintenance, timeout, or stop-boundary flags. MongoDB status validates immutable lineage, checksum-bound durable progress, and exact physical state.

symbols.name: ridu migrate verify
symbols.summary: Replay complete history in an isolated adapter-owned database and validate every intermediate state.
details: PostgreSQL verification uses a temporary shadow schema and accepts runner timeout controls but not stop boundaries. SQLite needs no deployment path and replays history, including registered compiled transforms, in a temporary database. MongoDB uses a command-scoped credential to create, replay, verify, and drop a random shadow database; use separate scoped credentials for the running application, verification, and backups.

symbols.name: ridu migrate up
symbols.summary: Validate complete history and apply pending artifacts under adapter-owned coordination.
details: PostgreSQL requires secure transport unless explicitly admitted, holds a session advisory lock, and resumes durable phased checkpoints. SQLite applies every pending artifact atomically under one BEGIN IMMEDIATE writer reservation. MongoDB requires verified TLS unless explicitly admitted for local development, holds a fenced expiring lease, and resumes checksum-bound durable steps.
symbols.example:
DATABASE_URL="$MONGODB_MIGRATION_URL" ridu migrate plan --json
# Drain every old application process, worker, and other writer.
DATABASE_URL="$MONGODB_OPERATIONAL_URL" ridu migrate verify
# Capture the matched database/upload snapshot.
DATABASE_URL="$MONGODB_MIGRATION_URL" ridu migrate up
DATABASE_URL="$MONGODB_MIGRATION_URL" ridu migrate status
# Start only the new digest; require /readyz before admitting traffic.
DATABASE_URL="$MONGODB_APP_URL" ./dist/content

symbols.name: ridu migrate down
symbols.summary: Reverse the latest applied SQLite artifact while retaining its immutable file.
details: SQLite only. The path may instead come from RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Status reports the reversed artifact as pending so migrate up can replay it.

symbols.name: ridu migrate reset
symbols.summary: Reverse every applied SQLite artifact in exact reverse order.
details: SQLite only. The path may instead come from RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Artifact files and checksums remain committed; schema, callbacks, and ledger changes roll back atomically.

symbols.name: ridu migrate refresh
symbols.summary: Reverse and replay complete committed SQLite history atomically.
details: SQLite only. The path may instead come from RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Registered compiled down and up callbacks run with their checksum-bound artifacts in the same transaction.

symbols.name: ridu migrate fresh
symbols.summary: Drop non-internal SQLite objects and replay committed history atomically.
details: SQLite only. The path may instead come from RIDU_SQLITE_PATH. Use this explicit destructive workflow for a reviewed local rebuild, not as production startup synchronization.

symbols.name: PostgreSQL migration runner options
symbols.summary: PostgreSQL operational admissions and bounds accepted by migrate up and, except stop boundaries, verify.
details: --allow-maintenance requires every application process and worker to remain stopped through completion and retries.
Zero durations select bounded defaults unless --allow-unbounded is explicit.
--stop-after-phase and --stop-after-step are accepted only by PostgreSQL migrate up; verify always runs to completion.

symbols.name: MongoDB migration runner options
symbols.summary: MongoDB operational admissions and bounds accepted by migrate up and verify.
details: --allow-maintenance requires every application process and worker to remain stopped through completion and retries.

--advisory-lock-wait bounds acquisition of the fenced migration lease; --concurrent-index-timeout bounds the complete MongoDB migration operation. Zero selects bounded defaults unless --allow-unbounded is explicit, and lease expiry remains bounded.

MongoDB rejects the PostgreSQL-only --lock-timeout, --statement-timeout, --batch-timeout, --idle-in-transaction-timeout, --stop-after-phase, and --stop-after-step controls. Interrupted work resumes from the checksum-bound durable step ledger.

symbols.name: ridu plugin new
symbols.summary: Scaffold paired Go and Svelte plugin packages with conformance tests.
details: The key must be stable and lowercase. Publish the Go and admin packages with matching plugin pairing versions after both conformance suites pass.
symbols.example:
ridu plugin new ./ridu-color \
	--key color \
	--module example.com/acme/ridu-color \
	--admin-package @acme/ridu-color-admin

symbols.name: ridu plugin add
symbols.summary: Install and register a compiled backend plugin and optional paired admin package.

parameters.name: --go-version
parameters.description: Go module requirement; defaults to latest.

parameters.name: --constructor
parameters.description: Exported zero-argument constructor; defaults to New.

parameters.name: --admin-version
parameters.description: Admin package requirement; defaults to latest.

parameters.name: --no-install
parameters.description: Update registration without invoking Go or the configured frontend package manager.

details: ridu add is an exact alias. The command updates dependencies and registration, regenerates contracts, checks compatibility, and rolls back its files on failure. Review the descriptor and create a migration afterward.

symbols.name: ridu plugin remove
symbols.summary: Remove static plugin registration and dependencies, then regenerate contracts.
details: Without --no-install the command removes the Bun dependency and runs go mod tidy. It rolls back on generation failure. Create a migration to review any plugin down steps.

symbols.name: ridu version
symbols.summary: Print the compiled CLI version.

symbols.name: ridu help
symbols.summary: Show commands and the compiled project-protocol and schema-manifest versions.
